content.prompt: Explain why the conjugate of $3-\sqrt{4}$ is not $3+\sqrt{4}$.

answer.short: $\sqrt{4}=2$, so $3-\sqrt{4}=1$ is rational and its conjugate is itself, $1$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}3-\sqrt{4}&=3-2\\3-\sqrt{4}&=1\end{align*}$$
The result is rational, so its conjugate is $1$. In contrast, $3+\sqrt{4}=5$.
